problems.problem: The first reading’s objection still stands: the batch keeps Numbers 6:7, the Nazirite’s ban on corpse uncleanness, when the day holds the Priestly Blessing (6:24 to 26). Its reading turns on nezer, crown, a link the English ‘consecration’ never shows the reader, so the image of the crowned king is left without its point, and half of it is a derivation Ibn Ezra only reports (ויש אומרים). The move to 6:26 (revise ~2) was refuted only on FORM, because its plain sense was a participial fragment with no main clause; its key, Rashi (יכבש כעסו) and Rashbam (שלא יסתיר פניו מכם ... ישא פנים שלו את אהובו שיפנה אליו לחננו) were re-found verbatim and the refuter found no drift.
